    - strong: Zero is not the same as absent.
    - text: Taoyuan Metro publishes a transfer dataset and it is empty — the Airport MRT has no in-system interchanges to record. An em dash means the operator does not publish that dataset at all.
  - heading "Ours — researched, not official" [level=2]
  - list:
    - listitem:
      - strong: Elevated or underground.
      - text: TDX does not publish structure. Ours is compiled by hand and kept in a separate overlay file so refetching official data can never overwrite it — and so it is never mistaken for official data. Two Wenhu stations are marked
      - emphasis: not established
      - text: rather than guessed.
    - listitem:
      - strong: Everything about rolling stock and depots.
      - text: Fleet sizes, car dimensions, capacities, depot areas and stabling capacity are not in any open dataset we have found. Anything marked TBC on those pages is genuinely unknown to us, not merely unfetched.
    - listitem:
      - strong: Measured route lengths.
      - text: Distances computed along the drawn geometry, between the first station and the last. These are ours, and they sit beside the operators' own figures on
      - link "the network page":
        - /url: /rail/network/
      - text: rather than replacing them — printing both is what makes the check visible.
  - heading "Corrected" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: This site previously said TDX did not publish route length, because the
    - code: RouteLength
    - text: "field on the route record is zero for every metro route. That was wrong, and the data was already in this repository:"
    - code: StationOfRoute
    - text: carries a cumulative distance against every station, and the last one is the route's length. The Wenhu Line is 25.17 km, which settles a figure this site had been recording as unsourced. The lesson is the same one the line colours taught — check the whole record before concluding a source is silent.
  - heading "Still open" [level=2]
  - list:
    - listitem: Which two Wenhu stations are underground.
    - listitem: Where the 25.7 km Wenhu route length in circulation comes from. The official figure is 25.17 km and our own measurement agrees at 25.04 km; 25.7 is unaccounted for.
    - listitem: Headways, track gauge and electrification.
    - listitem: Station opening dates — not published in any dataset we fetch.
    - listitem:
      - text: Whether DORTS's published Pantone and CMYK signage values match the hex values on
      - link "the colours page":
        - /url: /data/line-colours/
      - text: .
  - heading "Licence and reuse" [level=2]
  - paragraph:
    - text: The underlying records are Taiwan government open data, published by MOTC through TDX under the
    - link "Open Government Data Licence":
      - /url: https://data.gov.tw/licenses
    - text: . You may use, reproduce, distribute and adapt them, including commercially, provided you attribute the source.
  - paragraph: Our derived work — the contrast-checked badge and accent colours, the chained geometry, the structure overlay — is offered on the same terms. Attribution to Taipei Transit Guide is welcome but not required; attribution to MOTC is required by their licence, not ours.
  - paragraph: 180 TDX stations · 12 primary-sourced Sanying stations · 5 operators · retrieved 2026-08-10 · sources last updated 2020-01-31 to 2026-08-05

about.snapshot:
- main:
  - navigation "Breadcrumb":
    - link "Home":
      - /url: /
    - text: About
  - link "Back to the previous page":
    - /url: /data/provenance/
  - heading "About" [level=1]
  - paragraph: An English-language reference for public transport in Taipei, written because the material exists in Mandarin and nowhere else in a form you can look something up in.
  - heading "What this is" [level=2]
  - paragraph: Taipei's transport network is unusually well documented — in Mandarin. Between 批踢踢 (PTT), Mobile01 and the Chinese Wikipedia there is detailed, argued-over coverage of rolling stock, depot allocations, signalling contracts and construction history. Some of it is better than anything published officially.
  - paragraph: "In English there is an encyclopedia article per line and a great deal of visitor-facing advice about which exit to use. What is missing is the layer in between: structured reference material you can look a fact up in, with the source attached. That gap is what this site is for."
  - paragraph: It is independent and non-commercial. It is not affiliated with Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation, New Taipei Metro, Taoyuan Metro, the Taipei City Government or any bus operator, and it carries no advertising.
  - heading "How it sources material" [level=2]
  - heading "Official data where it exists" [level=3]
  - paragraph:
    - text: For the 180 stations the platform carries, names, codes, running order, coordinates, interchanges, route lengths and end-to-end times come from
    - link "TDX":
      - /url: https://tdx.transportdata.tw/
    - text: ", the Ministry of Transportation and Communications' open data platform. So do 9 of the 10 line colours, from the publishing operator's own line record. The exception is the Sanying Line, which opened in June 2026 and has no record on the platform at all; its colour was read instead from the operator's own line mark, and"
    - link "the line colours page":
      - /url: /data/line-colours/
    - text: says exactly which file and what it was checked against. TDX has no Sanying station dataset either, so LB01–LB12 are maintained in a separate hand-researched registry from the operator's station table and twelve information sheets. Every displayed Sanying fact links to that primary evidence, and coordinates remain TBC. The generated TDX registry itself is not hand-edited.
  - paragraph:
    - text: That decision has already paid for itself twice. Every English-language line colour we could find was wrong, including two cases where a confident correction citing an official map moved
    - emphasis: away
    - text: from the official value — the working is on
    - link "the colours page":
      - /url: /data/line-colours/
    - text: . And the route length this site published was 1.4 km too long, because it measured geometry that runs past both termini into depot leads, while the operator's own figure sat unread in a field nobody had looked in.
  - heading "Mandarin sources, synthesised rather than translated" [level=3]
  - paragraph: Where official data stops — fleet histories, depot facilities, the Matra contract dispute, why a line was built the way it was — the material is in Mandarin. The policy is to read it, cross-check it, and write it in English from scratch, citing the original in its own language rather than an English mirror of it. Translating a forum thread wholesale would be both a copyright problem and a way of importing its errors without noticing them.
  - paragraph: Where sources disagree, the intention is to record every value rather than pick the most plausible one and present it as settled.
  - heading "TBC rather than a guess" [level=3]
  - paragraph:
    - text: A figure marked
    - emphasis: TBC
    - text: means nobody here has traced it to a source worth citing. It does not mean the number is unknown to the world. It would be easy to fill those gaps with figures that are probably right, and the site would look more finished; it would also stop being usable as a reference, because you could no longer tell which numbers had been checked.
  - paragraph:
    - text: The same applies structurally. The
    - link "bus section":
      - /url: /bus/
    - text: is empty and says so rather than being hidden. Where a figure has been settled since — the two underground Wenhu stations were marked “not established” for four builds and are now named, from the builder’s own record and an encyclopedia agreeing from different directions — the page says how it was settled rather than quietly filling the gap.
  - heading "Citations, and a count of what has none" [level=3]
  - paragraph:
    - text: Every page carries a source list, and a figure that rests on one says so with a numbered mark you can follow. Each entry records the title in English and in the original language, the publisher, the date the URL was read, and whether the source is
    - strong: primary
    - text: — the operator, the builder, a government department, a court — or
    - strong: secondary
    - text: ". That last field is required and has no default: this site has already found a case where a citation to an official route map was further from the published colour than the value it replaced, so who says a thing has to travel with the thing."
  - paragraph:
    - text: Everything cited anywhere is collected in the
    - link "bibliography":
      - /url: /data/sources/
    - text: ", with the primary-to-secondary ratio stated at the top. It is currently about a third primary, which is not good enough and is published anyway."
  - paragraph:
    - text: The build also counts statements that carry
    - emphasis: "no"
    - text: source at all, separately from those marked TBC, and refuses to let that number grow. A labelled gap and an unlabelled assertion are different failures, and only one of them is honest.
  - heading "What is not used" [level=3]
  - paragraph: No operator's route map, photography or signage artwork. Those are copyrighted. The maps on this site are drawn from published coordinate geometry, and the line colours are the published hex values — a colour specification is a fact, an operator's specific map is a design.
  - paragraph:
    - link "Data provenance":
      - /url: /data/provenance/
    - text: sets out field by field what is official, what is researched here, what is derived, and what is still open.
  - heading "Where it has got to" [level=2]
  - paragraph: This is version 1. Every line now has a page written from primary sources, and the Wenhu Line — the first one built, and the one this site went deepest on — also has a page per station, built from official records. 4 of the 98 written pages still carry a stub flag, meaning some figures on them still need tracing to a primary source.
  - paragraph:
    - text: All 192 stations across the network are registered, so any station code on the site validates and any of them can be looked up on
    - link "the station records page":
      - /url: /data/stations/
    - text: ", and every one of them now has a page of its own — position, district, coordinates, interchanges, and run times where its source publishes them. Wenhu's 24 go further: TDX does not publish structure, street exits or engineering numbers, so those come from a hand-built overlay, plus a photograph for every station. A station on another line is a plain TDX read until someone researches it the way Wenhu was researched. Sanying's 12 are the other exception: primary-sourced station records, with unavailable fields shown as TBC rather than inferred from maps."
  - heading "Corrections" [level=2]
  - paragraph: "Corrections are welcome, and specific ones are most useful: the page, the figure, and what it should be, with a source. A source in Mandarin is as good as one in English, and often better."
  - paragraph: The most valuable corrections are the ones that catch something stated confidently and wrongly, rather than something already marked TBC — a gap that is labelled is doing its job, but a wrong figure presented as checked undermines everything next to it.
  - paragraph:
    - strong: Reporting a correction.
    - text: Open an issue on the repository this site is built from, quoting the page URL and the figure in question. If you would rather not use an issue tracker, the same information sent any other way is just as welcome — what matters is the source, not the channel.
  - heading "How it is built" [level=2]
  - paragraph: Content is Markdown; the site is generated as static HTML and served as files, with no server and no runtime API calls. Station code badges, Chinese language tagging, strip maps and geographic maps are all produced at build time from the data, which is why a station code that is not real fails the build rather than rendering as though it were.
  - paragraph: Station and line data retrieved from MOTC TDX on 2026-08-10. Government open data, used under the Open Government Data Licence.
